NOTE (Wed 22 Jul, ~11:26 BST, Bath) — Burnham ordered new Justice Secretary Alex Norris to review the Sentencing Act early-release scheme (from Sept, thousands of offenders in England & Wales eligible for earlier release) after outrage that two of PC Andrew Harper's killers could be freed halfway through 13-year manslaughter terms. Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers may qualify; driver Henry Long (16 yrs) will NOT. Burnham: "All I can say is I will review the whole of this policy. Nobody can deny the pressure on prison places. But I want to assure myself that everything has been looked at before this policy proceeds... every single part of this I will look into with the justice secretary." / "I feel for the family, it's an appalling crime that was committed. The main perpetrator will not be subject to any early release." / "I can't say that I can change the policy completely, but I will look at it in detail before we go further forward."
Harper's widow: early release "deplorable"; his mother: it feels like an "insult". Thames Valley PCC Matthew Barber wrote to PM/Lord Chancellor urging emergency legislation: "The killers of Andrew Harper should remain in prison and should not be released early." Shadow justice minister Nick Timothy: "Labour's early release scheme has been catastrophic. Victims should not have to live in fear all summer waiting for a review... It would be shameful if the killers of PC Andrew Harper, grooming gang perpetrators and rapists were to get out of prison early." Victim Support CEO Katie Kempen urged the review be done "urgently". (Parliament in recess — this is an executive review, not Commons business.)
